passage: Alka, you keep asking why your Himani Ma'am keeps a red bag behind the office door. Sit, I'll tell you. Twelve years ago I was twenty-five, renting a room near the river in Silchar with my younger sister. In the first flood that year, we spent forty minutes in the dark hunting for her college certificates and her inhaler while the water climbed the stairs. After that, I packed one bag and kept it by the door: photocopies of our documents in a zip pouch, a strip of each medicine, two thousand in small notes, a torch, spare batteries, a charger and a power bank I topped up every Sunday. The next flood came in July. I woke my sister, lifted the bag, locked the door. Six minutes, Alka. We didn't have to decide anything.

'What goes first?' she said, half to Siddharth. 'Stock on the bottom shelves: notebooks, chart paper. All ruined in an hour. So the heavy stock goes up to the top racks now, and the bottom two stay empty till October.'

'Then school orders by phone. You deliver on the scooter when roads open. I'll tell the regular schools this week.'

12 August, 11 p.m., Mama's house, Kolhapur
I'm writing this on a borrowed mattress because my hands won't stop shaking. The alert came at five. We all said the same thing: Akash Kaka will tell us what to do. He always does. He has the car, he knows the relief office people. So we waited for his call. At six his phone was out of network. We kept calling. Aaji asked where we were meeting. Nobody knew. Papa thought the temple hall, I thought Akash Kaka's building. We lost three hours going between the two in the rain, with Aaji on the back of the scooter. We finally found each other here at nine, soaked. Tomorrow I'm writing a family meeting point on paper for every single one of us, and a second number to call.

Elizabeth nodded. 'And if the rest of the claim comes?'

Hi Samir,
You said on Sunday you'd got a scary email from the tax department and wanted to call a CA at once. Let me tell you what I did in March when I got one, because I nearly panicked too.
I didn't reply, didn't click anything, didn't even call Papa. I read it three times with a pen and paper. Who sent it? The address ended in the official domain, and it quoted my PAN correctly. What was it asking? It said one interest amount in my bank's statement didn't match my return, and asked me to confirm or explain. By when? Thirty days from the date of the email.
Once I'd written those three answers down, it stopped feeling like an accusation. It was a question with a deadline. I checked it on the portal, then made a plan.
Take a breath first. Then the pen.
Raghav

qa.a: Thirty days from the date of the email.

qa.a: Raghav moved from near panic to calm, because the email stopped feeling like an accusation and became a question with a deadline.

qa.q: What else could Samir do after reading the email carefully?
qa.a: Samir could check the notice on the official portal and, if it is unclear, take it to a chartered accountant with the three answers already written down.

qa.q: How might Samir feel reading Raghav's email?
qa.a: Samir may feel reassured and less alone, since a friend admits nearly panicking too and shows a simple way to start.

grounding: It shows someone reading a tax department email for who sent it, what it asks and the last date, and waiting until the facts are clear before reacting.

Tuesday night
Spread everything on the bed tonight: twelve salary slips, the Form 16 from the office, two bank statements, and the notice that's been scaring me since Friday. Jahnavi di sat with me with a highlighter, which made it bearable.
The notice says my income was 2,40,000 more than I declared. Impossible. So, one line at a time: the salary slips add up to exactly what's in the Form 16. Bank statements: salary credits match every month. Then Jahnavi di spotted it. The notice lists my salary under the old company AND the same amount again under a new employer code. The company was bought and renamed in October; I never changed jobs. Same money, counted twice.
I can breathe again. Tomorrow I'll write it up with the two slips side by side and ask the CA uncle to check my reply.
Irawati
